title: Normalized cohomology maps satisfy the diagram and cocone laws.

from.place: Proof: continuity for the punctured-neighborhood inverse system, using Cohomology Tag 0A37; laws subargument.

statement: Let I be a nonempty directed preorder and let S_i and X be topological spaces. Give continuous maps f_ij:S_j→S_i for i≤j with f_ii=id and f_ij∘f_jk=f_ik, and continuous maps p_i:X→S_i with f_ij∘p_j=p_i. Give abelian sheaves F_i, f-maps α_ij:F_i→(f_ij)_*F_j, and require α_ii=id and α_ik=(f_ij)_*α_jk∘α_ij on every open section. Let P:I→Sh(X,Ab) have a colimit F and isomorphisms P_i≅p_i⁻¹F_i [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image, def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Require the transition P_i→P_j to send the unit of each section s of F_i to the unit of α_ij(s), after the canonical equality of inverse-image opens. Cohomology means Ext from the free abelian sheaf of an open [def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology]. For each transition and projection fix a family of cohomology pullbacks [lem-weil-pbc-site-cohomology-pullback-data], natural in the sheaf, compatible with Yoneda connecting maps, and equal in degree zero to the adjunction unit. For an f-map A → h_*B write m(h,A→h_*B,q) [def-weil-pbc-spectral-limit-cohomology-map] for pullback to h⁻¹A followed by the map induced by its adjoint h⁻¹A → B and by restriction along h⁻¹(top)=top. Write b_i for m(p_i,F_i→(p_i)_*F,q), where this f-map is adjoint to the coprojection p_i⁻¹F_i→F. Then, for every degree q≥0, the maps a_ij=m(f_ij,α_ij,q) satisfy a_ii=id, a_jk∘a_ij=a_ik, and b_j∘a_ij=b_i. No spectrality or inverse-limit hypothesis is assumed. The three equations are packaged as the proposition CohomologyMapLaws [def-weil-pbc-spectral-limit-cohomology-laws].

source.place: Tag 0A37, label lemma-colimit, induction and comparison argument

proof.text: For each continuous map h, exact inverse image makes A↦H^n(h⁻¹A) a cohomological delta-functor. The given normalized family commutes with its Yoneda connecting maps. Embed A into an injective I with quotient Q. Positive cohomology of I vanishes, so the connecting map H^n(Q)→H^(n+1)(A) is surjective. Consequently two natural, boundary-compatible families with the same degree-zero values are equal, by induction on n. This argument also applies after composing with exact inverse-image functors and natural coefficient maps.

source.place: Tag 0A37, label lemma-colimit, final sentence and preceding setup, specialized to a directed-set index

proof.text: Use the proved canonical-map evaluation formula and Mathlib’s adjunction hom-equivalence unit equation. They give the section formulas required by the injective-evaluation transfer lemma, with M_i=H^0(S_i,F_i), N=H^0(X,colim P), and generator evaluation. Its injectivity gives the identity, composition and cocone equations in degree zero. Instantiating this interface at the concrete cohomology groups is part of this remaining laws obligation.

source.place: Tag 0A37, label lemma-colimit, final sentence and preceding setup, specialized to a directed-set index

proof.text: Apply the preceding uniqueness argument to identity pullback and to successive pullbacks. Their degree-zero maps are respectively identity and the composite of section maps; inverse-image composition is the unit-compatible isomorphism between the two left adjoints. Naturality in the sheaf and compatibility with boundaries are preserved by this isomorphism. Thus the identity and composite formulas hold in every degree. The hypotheses on α identify these formulas with a_ii=id and a_ij≫a_jk=a_ik.

source.place: Tag 0A37, label lemma-colimit, final sentence and preceding setup, specialized to a directed-set index

proof.text: For the legs, hP identifies the transition between pullback sheaves on every unit section. Adjunction says these units determine the coefficient arrow. Compose with the colimit coprojection and use its cocone equation. This identifies the composite f-map for f_ij then p_j with the leg for p_i on sections, hence in all degrees by the same normalized uniqueness argument. This is a_ij≫b_j=b_i.
